declared_wall_clock_telemetry_exemption_.finding: 4 raw substring hits, none a mechanized field-exemption list: (1) mission.md's own hypothesis sentence being tested here, (2) an unrelated Monte Carlo RNG-source disclaimer in reference/mvp20/out/run_manifest.json ('no wall-clock RNG source is used'), and (3-4) a single unrelated boolean flag 'wall_clock_used': false inside a DIFFERENT prior study's diagnostic (anchor-necessity-reforge-resistance-v1), which records whether THAT harness used wall-clock timing, not a declaration of which run-provenance archive fields may vary. Zero hits define an allowlist, schema field, or code constant naming which manifest.json/final-state.json/provenance.json fields are permitted to diverge under the hypothesis. There is no mechanism, shipped or documented, by which an auditor (or verify_run, or replay --verify) can distinguish 'declared wall-clock telemetry' from any other diverging byte.

hypothesis_under_test.text_verbatim: This module supports the decision of whether a complete validated run can be replayed from hash-bound inputs. Its falsifiable hypothesis is that fixed-seed replay is byte-identical outside declared wall-clock telemetry.

positive_finding: The underlying scientific content IS deterministic: after stripping run_id and the five named timing-telemetry field names (at_ms, started_at_ms, average_latency_ms, duration_ms, wall_clock_ms) by hand, all 22 real events (proposals, mutations, scores, rankings, result_hash values) are byte-identical between the two runs -- confirming the sha256-counter-v1 seeded RNG and scoring path genuinely replay deterministically at the content level. What is refuted is narrower and more consequential: the module's own root_hash/verify_run apparatus cannot witness that fact, because it hashes run_id (wall-clock-derived in production) and unlabelled real telemetry (average_latency_ms) into the SAME anchor it holds out as proof of byte-identical replay, with no declared separation.
refutation_criterion_verbatim: Two independent production `amphora-tui run` invocations (binary built from amphora-cli, workspace bin name amphora-tui) with identical --candidate, --seed, --population, --generations, --workers, --lane, and objective profile produce a DIFFERENT provenance.json root_hash (the module's sole content-addressable replay-identity anchor), and the divergent bytes are not confined to any field the module or its docs DECLARE as exempt wall-clock telemetry.

root_cause_source_read.interpretation: The module already contains a deterministic, seed-derived run identity function (deterministic_run_id, stable_hash over candidate+seed+population+generations+workers+lane+profile) and assigns it to scoring_run_id unconditionally. But the on-disk archive identity used for .amphora/runs/<run_id> (and therefore embedded byte-for-byte into manifest.json, into every event's run_id field in events.jsonl, and transitively into every provenance.json hash field) is scoring_run_id ONLY when demo==true. The production `run` subcommand (not `demo`) takes the else branch and uses format!("run-{}", now_ms()) instead -- wall-clock milliseconds -- even though nothing about population/generations/candidate/seed prevented reusing the deterministic id it already computed one line earlier.

shipped_replay_command_capability.finding: `amphora-tui replay --run <path> --verify` only re-runs verify_run against the ONE archive named; the CLI ships no subcommand that compares two archives, or a fresh run against a prior one, for replay-determinism. The falsifiable hypothesis as stated is therefore not testable by any tool the module ships -- this harness is the first artifact in the module's history to actually exercise it.
